chunks: And by his chain that, Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said

regarding a man who saw a bird, so he pursued it until it fell upon a tree. So another man came over, so he seized it. So Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'It is for the eye what it sees, and for the hand what it seizes'.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal principle regarding ownership of a hunted animal based on sight and seizure?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) articulates a foundational principle of property acquisition by distinguishing between the right of pursuit (tabi') and the right of actual possession (qabd). This ruling, recorded in al-Kafi, clarifies that while the initial observer has a claim, the one who physically secures the bird holds the definitive title, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence on hunting and movable goods. It underscores the importance of tangible action in establishing ownership rights within the community.

en.hubeali: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said regarding a man who saw a bird, so he pursued it until it fell upon a tree. So another man came over, so he seized it. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is for the eye what it sees, and for the hand what it seizes’.
en.sarwar: 6. Through the same chain of narrators as that of the previous Hadith

the following is narrated: “About a man who sees a bird and follows it until it sits on a tree and another man comes and takes it, ’Amir al-Mu 5 minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘For an eye is what it has seen and for hands is what they catch 5 ”
